title: Cockroach Janta Party Leaders Detained and Released Amid Delhi Protests
summary: Delhi saw a second day of protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Protests at Jantar Mantar and surrounding areas resulted in the detention of several leaders, with police enforcing strict security measures. The CJP accused the government of security violations, and leaders were released after being produced before a magistrate.

facts.statement: Delhi Police arrested Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, and Ajinkya Shinde for trespassing into the Jantar Mantar protest site, following a rally in the area.
The protesters, a group linked to the CJP, demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, citing security and political issues.
Leaders were released after being produced before a magistrate after the detention was enforced.

sources.title: Indian court orders release of two leaders of Cockroach movement
sources.description:
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown

An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests.

The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week.

sources.title: SEM court orders release of CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
sources.description: A special executive magistrate ordered the release of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka after their judicial custody expired in connection with the October 14 Jantar Mantar protest.

sources.title: Delhi HC to hear Neha Bora's plea against 'peace' bond on October 22
sources.description:

sources.title: Delhi HC denies relief to CJP leaders challenging judicial custody
sources.description:
Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Wednesday withdrew from the Delhi High Court their plea challenging the extension of their judicial custody by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM).
Justice Subramonium Prasad told the counsel appearing for the CJP co-conveners to await the outcome of the hearing scheduled before the SEM later in the day, and approach the appellate court if their grievance continues.
While permitting Das and Ranka to withdraw the case, the judge clarified that he has not made observations on the merit of the matter.
During the hearing, the court orally observed that a petition under Article 226 of the Constitution was not an appropriate remedy in this case.

sources.description:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday agreed to urgently hear Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's plea against the extension of their judicial custody by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM).
Justice Subramonium Prasad will also take up a separate petition by the All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora against a Delhi Police's October 17 notice asking her to execute a bond before a SEM for "keeping peace".

sources.title: Delhi Police transfers second case against CJP leaders' to Crime Branch
sources.description:
Delhi Police on Tuesday transferred another case registered against Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to the Crime Branch, sources said.
The Crime Branch will now investigate two cases against the CJP leaders. The other case linked to Das and Ranka allegedly entering the Jantar Mantar area was transferred to the Crime Branch on Monday.
According to Delhi Police, on October 13, Das, Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and 11 other members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) reached Jantar Mantar, which has been denotified as a designated protest site, by trespassing through private premises.
Police personnel deployed at the spot intervened and tried to stop them. All 14 people were detained and two FIRs were registered.
Das and Ranka were sent to five-day judicial custody on October 14 by a Special Executive Magistrate for breaching peace bonds. Their judicial custody was extended by two days on Monday.
